notes.title: Strange Antiquities is a perfect sequel that sent my witchy heart aflutter
notes.notes:
There's beauty in simplicity. While I love games that push me to my limits, sometimes curling up with a hot chocolate (pumpkin spice at this time of year, of course) and playing a good ol' visual novel is exactly what I need. I recently delved back into the World of Darkness with Vampire: The Masquerade - Reckoning of New York, followed by a brief stint brewing warm drinks in Coffee Talk. All of this, however, was in preparation for Strange Antiquities, the highly anticipated follow-up to Bad Viking's puzzle game turned detective story, Strange Horticulture. It's been three years since we last pet Jupiter the cat and tinkered around with potentially lethal leafy oddities, and a part of me wondered how Antiquities would set itself apart from its predecessor without suffering from feature bloat.

Read the rest of the story...

notes.title: The Thaumaturge’s Handbook: An FAQ for Strange Antiquities
notes.notes:
[h3][b]Dear Thaumaturges,[/b]
[/h3][p][/p][p]Before you set foot on the creaky floorboards of our shop on Hollowell Lane, we figured some of you still might have [b]a few questions about your role, the shop, and the journey ahead[/b]. In this blog, we’ll answer a handful of them to make sure you don’t cause someone’s demise during your very first shift.
[/p][p][b]Do I need to have played Strange Horticulture?[/b][/p][p]No. [i]Strange Antiquities[/i] is a [b]stand-alone sequel set in the same world but tells a completely separate story[/b]. Returning players will find [b]familiar mechanics and lore[/b], but the game has been designed to be welcoming for new players too. Take your time - discovery is part of the experience. And if you’re ever stuck, there’s a [b]hint button[/b] to help.
[/p][p][b]Will there be some familiar faces?[/b][/p][p]Yes. Previous visitors to Undermere may spot some [b]familiar customers, along with crossover lore, references, and Easter Eggs[/b] for fans of [i]Strange Horticulture[/i].[/p][p][/p][p][b]Will there be multiple endings again?[/b][/p][p]Yes! There are at least [b]8 distinct endings[/b] to discover. None of them are “wrong” - they’re simply reflections of the path you took.[/p][p][/p][p][b]What about the Closer Inspect system?[/b][/p][p]We’ve expanded the “Closer Inspect” mechanic so you can now [b]examine items in greater detail[/b]. There are four categories of analysis, and you can hover your mouse over different sections of each artefact to uncover useful information and hidden clues.[/p][p][/p][p][b]… and the new books?[/b][/p][p]You’ll find [b]several new tomes to study[/b], packed with hints and lore to help identify strange antiquities.[/p][p][/p][p][b]What else is new?[/b][/p][p]Err. [u][b]No more spoilers now[/b][/u] - you’ll have to play the game and discover the game’s secrets for yourself. [/p][p][/p][p][b]I need to know: can you still pet the cat?[/b][/p][p]Of course. His name is [b]Jupiter[/b]. [i]To be honest, if regular petting is not part of your daily ritual, then one might infer that you’re a monster.[/i][/p][p][/p][p][b]Eli White told me not to touch anything. I’m sure that means there are no secrets to discover, right?[/b][/p][p]Let's just say rules were meant to be broken... 😉 [/p][p][/p][p][b]What are the controls?[/b][/p][p]The game is fully playable with just a mouse.[/p][p]Right-click to inspect.[/p][p]Mouse wheel for magnifying glass. 
[/p][p]There are also keyboard shortcuts for those with a different play style.[/p][p]Arrow keys/WASD to move around the shop.[/p][p]Shift for magnifying glass[/p][p][/p][p][b]Is there controller support?[/b][/p][p]Yes.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Does it play well on Steam Deck?[/b][/p][p]Yes. Tested, tuned, and [b]Verified[/b] on Steam Deck![/p][p][/p][p][b]How long is the game?[/b][/p][p]Tricky to say. [b]6-10 hours, but possibly longer[/b], depending on how you play. [/p][p][/p][p][b]What is the price point?[/b][/p][p]$17.99 with a 10% launch discount[/p][p][/p][p][b]What engine does it run on?[/b][/p][p]Unity.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Do you plan to release it on additional platforms?[/b][/p][p]PC and Nintendo Switch at launch. More platforms to follow in due course.
[/p][p][b]What about Mac?[/b][/p][p]Mac is a [b]priority[/b] for us, but we couldn’t get it ready in time for launch. Please bear with us - we’ll update you as soon as we can…[/p][p][/p][p][b]What are the accessibility options?[/b][/p][list][*][p]Easy-to-read [b]fonts[/b][/p][/*][*][p]Zoom with the [b]Magnifying Glass[/b] [/p][/*][*][p]“Closer Inspect” descriptions include [b]colour cues[/b] - we’re colourblind ourselves, and we’ve tried to make sure fellow colour-impaired folk can play comfortably. [/p][/*][*][p]Mouse-only controls, but with added keyboard support.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Arachnophia setting[/b] - there’s a small spider who sometimes wanders around the clock. His name is Tony. He’s harmless… but you can toggle him off if you’d prefer not to see him.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][b]What languages is the game in?[/b][/p][p]At launch: [b]English, French, German, Italian, Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese, Polish, Turkish, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Russian.[/b]
[/p][p][b]I want to cover the game on my channel/blog/outlet. How do I get a key?[/b][/p][p]For any coverage inquiries, just send an email to [u][i][b]pr\[at]iceberg-games\[dot]com[/b][/i][/u]! [/p][p][/p][p][b]Where do I report bugs if I find one?[/b][/p][p]You can report any bugs and hiccups [b]in our Steam forum[/b]. We’ll set up a dedicated bug-reproting thread here. 

[b]I uncovered some haunted antiquities in my grandpa’s attic. What do I do?[/b][/p][p]Apprentice at Strange Antiquities, and you’ll soon learn that every object has its uses… and its dangers.[/p][p]

notes.title: Undermere Herald - September Edition | Looking Back at Gamescom!
notes.notes:
[p][b]Dear Thaumaturges,[/b]
[/p][p]Our team left the halls of [b]Gamescom a little over a week ago[/b] and what a blast we had! Our ears are still ringing a little bit, but we can’t overstate how fun it was to travel all the way to [b]Cologne to meet a bunch of you and introduce Undermere to new players.[/b][/p][p]With our friends at Iceberg Interactive, we set up shop in a little corner of [b]Hall 10.2, alongside a mass of other exciting indies![/b] [/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45031160/365507c65536ba3aad91e890743503a5b5d8dfb4.jpg"][/img][/p][p]After 5 exhausting days, we’d gone through [b]copious press meetings, exciting demos, thrilling conversations with other devs[/b] and, notably, [i]countless cups of coffee and cans of soda[/i]. It felt more like a marathon, than a sprint, and, despite the lack of sleep, we really enjoyed ourselves[/p][p]But for us, the best part was [b]meeting all of [i]you[/i][/b]. On the one hand, we were able to introduce a bunch of new players to our shop. Frankly, we couldn’t have done that without Jupiter, so [b]he’ll be getting extra pets this week[/b]. On the other hand, it was really touching [b]to talk to members of our community and people who have played Strange Horticulture[/b]. Hearing your stories and talking about what the game means to all of us was an unforgettable experience. [b]Some people even came by with incredible DIY projects![/b] [/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45031160/d41736bc73a09a1c41e994b8681a56a57044895a.jpg"][/img][/p][p]All in all, we want to thank everyone for an [b]unforgettable gamescom![/b] Thanks to everyone who came by to play or chat! Thanks to [b]Indie Arena Booth, Nintendo, and every single one of the hardworking volunteers![/b] Thanks to our team and all the friends we made along the way! Being out there and talking about Strange Antiquities was a riot. [/p][p]For now, we’ll [b]retreat back into our developer caves and put some finishing touches on Strange Antiquities[/b]. notes.notes: Like a diabolical shopkeeper awaiting his first victim—sorry—customer of the day, I've been eagerly anticipating the release of Strange Antiquities since it was announced last year. The follow-up to 2022's Strange Horticulture lets players get their Needful Things on, selling eldritch antiques to an array of weird townsfolk. And it turns out the Lake District's most accused curiosity shop is opening its doors sooner than I expected, as Strange Antiquities launches next month... Read more.

Undermere is a unique little place. In Bad Viking's debut game, Strange Horticulture, its residents were embroiled in the peculiar machinations of a forest cult intent on summoning the mysterious Woken Dendrue. This ill omen is good news for you, though - as the temporary proprietor of local curios store Strange Antiquities, you're the first port of call for protection totems, warding spells, and mood-lifting enchantments. notes.title: Undermere Herald - May Edition | Meet Some Of Our Occult Locals
notes.notes:
[h3]Dear reader,[/h3]

Welcome to the May edition of the Undermere Herald - [b]the most trustworthy news source for Undermere and its surroundings. [/b]

We don’t know what it is about Undermere, but [b]something about our quaint little town attracts people seeking the thrill of the unknown.[/b] Some are adventurers, some are researchers - all have a hand in a world that few of us are familiar with. A world that lies behind dark curtains and buried in cold tombs.

In this month’s edition of the Herald, our reporters had a chat with some of our more esoteric inhabitants. [b]You can read about their work, their connection to the occult… and maybe a sentence or two about the content of their character.[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45031160/c750532448234d9959ec6e29b59870d262e18185.png[/img]
Few in Undermere deserve the title ‘thrillseeker’ more than Barton Potter. A self-styled Relic Hunter, Potter has traversed the peaks of our hills and the depths of our catacombs, [b]in search of the unusual and the arcane.[/b] He will gladly tell anyone who asks the story of how he lost the sight in his left eye, but it is [b]never clear how much is true and how much is embellished to suit the ear of the listener.[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45031160/8431f38552e283c15f15933227b84fe5f79be7d2.png[/img]
Only the more unfortunate among you will be familiar with Dr. Francesca Robertson. [b]She is not a doctor in the traditional sense…[/b] After a family tragedy, Dr. Robertson started looking for answers beyond the traditional textbooks, becoming [b]one of the region’s foremost experts on occult maladies[/b]. When Noctic Sight invades your dreams or Morgan’s Insanity threatens to unpick your hold on reality, Dr. Robertson is the person you most want on your side.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45031160/dfc8e539302dfb67d737272cafc8e1015e426a27.png[/img]
To say that [b]Undermere would look very different without Verona Green would be an understatement[/b]. The Occult Scholar is an esteemed member of our community. Kind and humble, yes, but sharp of mind and not someone to underestimate. It is hard to imagine a more fitting figurehead for our town, [b]but she would never accept a position of governance.[/b]

These are [b]but a handful of our most arcanely attuned townsfolk[/b]. As we delve deeper into the mysteries that surround us, we invite you to reflect on the unseen threads that may connect you to the world behind the veil.[b] We’d be curious to read about your connection to the occult in a reader’s letter![/b]

notes.title: Undermere Herald - March Edition | Literary Inspirations & A Guessing Game
notes.notes:
[h3]Dear reader,[/h3]

Welcome to the March edition of the Undermere Herald - [b]the most trustworthy news source for Undermere and its surroundings.[/b]

Since you’re holding this physical newspaper in your hand right now, we’ll assume that you, just like the writing staff here at the Herald, are an avid reader! From the rich tomes of Dickens to the pastoral poems of Wordsworth & Coleridge, the literary arts are a rich well of creative inspiration. This month, [b]we’ll discuss the works that inspire us.[/b]

[u][b]Strange Antiquities’ (Literary) Inspirations[/b][/u]

It’s hard to pinpoint specific inspirations for the world of Undermere because we’ve [b]drawn from such a wide range of our interests[/b], and there’s no one clear ‘main’ influence, but we’re going to try and break down some of those inspirations here.

Clearly, there is a [b]Lovecraftian angle[/b], but, like many modern Lovecraft-inspired works, it’s more of a distilled inspiration. Perhaps the main influence here is [b][url=https://boardgamegeek.com/boardgame/146021/eldritch-horror]a board game called Eldritch Horror[/url][/b] in which players battle against fearsome entities from other dimensions. The general ‘feel’ of the world, [b]from the story vignettes when you visit locations, to the Dread/Sanity system,[/b] certainly takes inspiration from that game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45031160/1743c0377fcdf10345abdd4a336f069b776087a1.jpg[/img]
Other smaller inspirations include [b]Granny Weatherwax from Terry Pratchett's Discworld novels[/b] who is channeled through the no-nonsense Verona Green. And then there are the green-eyed Draer who are [b]a nod to the blue-eyed Fremen from Frank Herbert's sci-fi epic, Dune[/b].

Keen-eyed observers with a bit of local knowledge will also be able to spot several Lake District-based references, whether that be from[b] local lore such as the witch Long Meg or the skulls of Calgarth Hall[/b], or in the [b]names of people and places[/b], such as Barton Potter, Wainwright Hospital, and Naylor Island.

[u][b]Can You Guess The Item? [/b][/u]

Before we let you go, readers, [b]here’s a little challenge:[/b] Strange Antiquities is all about occult artefacts. Here are just a handful of the carefully designed items from the game. One of these is a [b]Shadow Hold, which any Thaumaturge could tell you is for drawing out the manifestation known as Creeping Dark[/b], but can you guess which one?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45031160/04ab57a5f3aa4196e7927d777c9b2ee27de70332.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45031160/308ed3f1f57d363d52d31f4bb5c0f006419cf754.png[/img]

notes.title: Undermere Herald - August Edition | Jupiter & Puzzle Design
notes.notes:
[h3]Dear reader,[/h3]

Welcome to the August edition of the Undermere Herald - [b]the most trustworthy news source for Undermere and its surroundings. [/b]

As we’re nearing the end of the dog days of summer, it’s time to accustom ourselves to the coming of muckier weather. In today’s edition of the Herald, we’ll familiarise ourselves with one of Undermere’s [b]most famous felines, while peeking behind the curtain of the shop he resides in — Strange Antiquities![/b]

[u][b]Jupiter[/b][/u]

Jupiter is the Thaumaturge's cat. Or, [i]perhaps more accurately[/i], Eli is Jupiter's Thaumaturge. Jupiter found Strange Antiquities, perhaps drawn by the curiosities within, and made it his home. Eli was more than happy to accommodate him, but he learned early on that [b]Jupiter was his own master[/b].

His business is his own, but it largely consists of regular naps, terrorising rodents, and midnight explorations of Undermere and beyond. What he does on his excursions is a mystery, but he seems to be [b]well-known among the residents of Undermere[/b].

We named Jupiter after a lengthy brainstorming discussion where we explored the game’s themes to find something appropriate. We liked Jupiter because, as well as being associated with both astrology and alchemy, it is also the name of the cat in [b]Robin Jarvis'[/b] excellent Deptford Mice series of books which we enjoyed as kids.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45031160/afbff8cd536441e2c5be2654f13024f14bc12c20.png[/img]
[i]Image 1: Jupiter – king of naps and death of rats[/i]

[u][b]A Short Discussion on Puzzles[/b][/u]

Those of you who have played Strange Horticulture [b]will find the gameplay of Strange Antiquities familiar[/b]. The core of the game involves serving customers by using your detective skills to identify an item on your shelves. If you’re thinking, [i]‘but plants all have similar visual properties whereas items all look quite different so surely they’ll be easy to tell apart,’[/i] you’d be [b]absolutely right![/b] This has been one of the main challenges we’ve faced while developing the game, but we find that these sorts of constraints can push us to be more creative and we’ve been able to take that central gameplay concept a lot further than we did in Strange Horticulture.

That means as a player you might expect to [b]need to do a little more detective work this time around[/b], perhaps flicking through your well-worn copy of Hermetic Symbology to track down a relevant symbol, or [b]cross-referencing[/b] with a book on gemstones to learn which Thaumic discipline Bloodstone belongs to. We’ve still got some tweaking to do to make sure the difficulty is where we want it to be, but we’re excited for you to get your hands on it and find out what you make of it!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45031160/6dc0e212ddf0cb3cee01a82f4c2a935e05589599.png[/img]
[i]Image 2. An excerpt from 'Gemstones and their Thaumic Properties'[/i]

[u][b]Strange Words[/b][/u]

notes.title: Undermere Herald - July Edition | The Pitt Rivers museum and The Thaumaturge!
notes.notes:
[h3]Dear reader,[/h3]

Welcome to the inaugural edition of the Undermere Herald - [b]the most trustworthy news source for Undermere and its surroundings[/b]. In today’s edition, we will delve into the archaeological offerings of the University of Oxford’s [i]Pitt Rivers Museum[/i] and introduce one of the town’s most sought-after tradespeople: the Thaumaturge, Eli White. 

[u][b]Visiting the Pitt Rivers Museum:[/b][/u]

As John and I live in different parts of the UK, it's sometimes a challenge to get together for anything work-related. The item designs have been one of the biggest challenges for us on Strange Antiquities, so we felt there was a good opportunity for us to get out of the office and go for a field trip! 

We’re lucky enough to live within a couple of hours of some excellent museums, including everything that London has to offer, so we were spoiled for choice, but [b]the one that excited us the most was Oxford’s unique Pitt Rivers museum[/b]. It has an amazing collection of trinkets, curiosities, and artefacts from all over the world, all piled high in glass cabinets with handwritten labels, and mostly all in one big room. It’s very Strange Antiquities.

Going to Oxford also meant that we got two museums for the price of one – the Ashmolean is just down the road from the Pitt Rivers and is equally stuffed full of treasures. We had a great trip and came back buzzing with inspiration.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45031160/1a3fbdcd4b28d62510504218a4eed2225e46e339.jpg[/img]
[i]Image 1. A silvered, stoppered bottle said to contain a witch.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45031160/397e94a6aed674921b888c339bd10d7fb087c2d0.jpg[/img]
                          [i]Image 2. The stacked cabinets of the Pitt Rivers[/i]⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀

[u][b]Meet the Shopkeeper:[/b][/u]

Unlike in Strange Horticulture, you are not the owner of the shop in Strange Antiquities. That role belongs to Eli White, local Thaumaturge and collector of Objects. Objects that to the untrained eye may appear dull and lifeless, but that in the right hands, and armed with the right knowledge, can be a gateway to so much more. For Eli, the quest to unearth and understand each new Object has been the driving force of his adult life.

As his apprentice you still have a lot to learn, but when Eli is called away to help with an important matter, he reluctantly leaves you in charge. He is a stern master who knows first-hand what can happen if the right precautions are not taken. He doesn’t tend to show much emotion, but he does have a more tender side – a side that is mostly reserved for the store’s cat, Jupiter.

notes.title: Strange things are happening in Undermere…
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45031160/6427c433406768a58e06989056775d8c6aa4df9c.gif[/img]

Taking place several years after the events of Strange Horticulture, [b]Strange Antiquities is a new, dark, and cosy standalone adventure[/b] set in the world of Undermere. It is a place of ancient woodland, candle-lit libraries, and macabre folklore, where strange things happen as often as it rains.

You are the Thaumaturge’s apprentice, tasked with running a shop dealing in occult antiquities. When hundreds of ravens start circling over the town of Undermere, those in the know become concerned. Occult Scholar Verona Green visits Strange Antiquities to enquire about the unnatural series of events. But before she is able to meet with the Thaumaturge, [i]events take a sinister turn…[/i]
